detail: Reference solutions (float64, tol 1e-8) and the old production path.
verdict: pca1k full CV in 29 s on 32 threads (21 s on unscaled X); the old LassoCV code path takes 443 to 651 s on the same data. Unit-basis reference runs still in the queue.

detail: State-of-the-art CPU solver for p >> n; the yardstick for GPU work.
verdict: unit-100k full CV takes 403 s on 32 threads (reliable R2 0.326, 129 nonzeros). That is the CPU reference: the GPU working set gets the same answer in 34 s. unit-800k still running.

detail: Lasso has to justify itself against Ridge on test R2 in the unit basis.
verdict: Fixed. Ridge beats Lasso on PCA features (reliable R2 0.352 vs 0.309 on pca1k-raw). On layer1 units (unit-800k, 64 channels) it reaches 0.125. No Ridge run on unit-100k yet, so the unit-basis Lasso-vs-Ridge question is still open.

detail: Old runs used unscaled PCA columns (std 1 to 48); suspected cause of slow, non-converging fits.
verdict: Depends on the basis. PCA features: z-scoring hurts both Lasso (0.309 -> 0.258) and Ridge (0.352 -> 0.003). Layer1 units: z-scoring helps Ridge (0.076 raw -> 0.125). Unit-basis Lasso comparison not run yet.

detail: Old use ran 500 tiny fits one at a time and was far slower than CPU.

idea: Batched FISTA over targets x alphas
detail: Two big matmuls per iteration, restart, per-problem gap stopping, float32 vs float64.
verdict: Small-p solver only. pca1k CV in 2.4 s, but one path on unit-100k takes 553 s on H200 and still misses gap 1e-4 (reaches 8e-4), against 39 s for the working set. Screened variant still running.

detail: The plain deep-learning optimizer route; only option when X does not fit on the GPU.
verdict: unit-100k full CV: 300 epochs gives reliable R2 0.361 in 81 s with 1020 nonzeros; 1000 epochs gives 0.330 in 191 s with 447. Exact Lasso: 0.326 with 129 nonzeros in 34 s. Predicts as well or better when stopped early, but is 3 to 8x less sparse, slower, and far from the Lasso optimum (relative gap 0.6 to 2.6).

idea: w = u*v reparametrization with weight decay
detail: Smooth objective whose minima match the Lasso; exact-zero seeking without a prox step.
verdict: Closest to the exact solution among gradient methods: relative gap 0.018 after 1000 epochs (40 s path on unit-100k). No CV run yet.

detail: Simplest gradient variant; sparsity only after post-hoc thresholding.
verdict: Relative gap 0.81 after 1000 epochs on unit-100k (31 s path). No CV run yet.

idea: GPU-screened working set, small Gram subproblems
detail: GPU computes X'R for all targets; each problem is solved on a few hundred features. Expected front-runner.
verdict: Front-runner. unit-100k full CV in 34 s on H200, 12x faster than celer on 32 CPU threads (403 s) with identical R2 and sparsity. unit-800k with 383 channels in 76 s. A100 runs were 3 to 5x slower; cause not yet explained.

detail: Better dual points for earlier stopping and tighter screening, as in celer.
verdict: Implemented in the working-set inner solver (5 iterates, accepted only if the objective drops). Its separate contribution is not yet measured.

idea: Batch the CV folds into one solve
detail: Fold masks as row weights or Gram downdates so all 6 fits share work.
verdict: Implemented inside the working-set solver: folds are row-masked problems sharing X and one union Gram per fold. Its separate contribution is not yet measured.

idea: Woodbury ADMM with one shared n x n Cholesky
detail: One factorization serves every target and alpha; fast low-accuracy solutions.
verdict: Path to gap 1e-4 in 7.8 s (pca1k) and 51 s (unit-100k) on H200, against 39 s for the working set on unit-100k. No CV runs yet.

detail: Exploits second-order sparsity when active sets are small; optional stretch.

idea: Factorized readout: spatially sparse x feature-wise dense
detail: Changes the model, not just the solver; parked until the Lasso benchmark is settled.
